content.footnotes_and_references: See online Supplementary Data for emergency management algorithm. Refer to Table 8 for definition of high/intermediate-high/intermediate-low/low-risk PE. Cancer, heart failure and chronic lung disease are included in PESI and sPESI. See Supplementary Data Table 12 for the Hestia criteria. Prognostically relevant imaging (TTE or CTPA) findings in patients with acute PE are presented in Figure 3. A cardiac troponin test may already have been performed during initial diagnostic work-up.
content.hestia_exclusion_criteria_summary: The Hestia exclusion criteria (Supplementary Data Table 12) are a bedside checklist of clinical parameters/questions integrating PE severity, comorbidity and feasibility of home treatment. If any question is answered yes, the patient cannot be discharged early.

trial_results_and_outcomes.single_arm_home_treatment: In a single-arm management trial selecting candidates for home treatment using Hestia criteria, the 3-month recurrent VTE rate was 2.0% (95% CI approximately 0.8%–4.3%) in patients with acute PE discharged within 24 hours.
trial_results_and_outcomes.non_inferiority_trial_550_patients: A non-inferiority trial randomized 550 patients to direct discharge based on Hestia criteria alone versus Hestia plus NT-proBNP testing and discharge if NT-proBNP ≤500 pg/mL. The primary outcome (30-day PE- or bleeding-related mortality, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or ICU admission) was very low in both arms; no incremental value of natriuretic-peptide testing was demonstrated for patients eligible for home treatment by Hestia criteria.
trial_results_and_outcomes.pesi_spesi_trial_344_patients: In a trial of 344 patients randomized to inpatient vs outpatient treatment using PESI in combination with feasibility criteria, one patient (0.6%) in each treatment group died within 90 days.
trial_results_and_outcomes.prospective_cohort_outcomes: In patients treated at home (with or without short hospitalization), 3-month rates were: thromboembolic recurrence 1.75%, major bleeding 1.43%, and death 2.83%.

content.pesi_and_spesi_summary: PESI and its simplified form sPESI integrate clinical parameters of PE severity and comorbidity to assess overall 30-day mortality. PESI is more standardized but less comprehensive regarding aggravating conditions compared with Hestia. sPESI excludes all patients with cancer from the low-risk category. PESI was not primarily developed to select candidates for home treatment but has been used with additional feasibility criteria.
biomarkers_and_tests_mentioned: NT-proBNP testing (natriuretic peptide) with reported threshold ≤500 pg/mL in a trial context
prognostically relevant imaging: TTE or CTPA
content.conclusion: Available evidence indicates both the Hestia rule and PESI/sPESI are capable of reliably identifying patients who are (i) at low PE-related risk and (ii) free of serious comorbidity, and therefore candidates for consideration of early discharge or outpatient treatment.
